package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects the version running on Smith & Wesson's website at the time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is designed to steal customer payment data by skimming sensitive information from the checkout process and exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled server. This is a classic example of a web skimmer/magecart-style attack, which is always considered malicious as it directly targets user financial data.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into Magento website frontend JavaScript (likely in a payment or checkout template file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the form submission event on the checkout page, collects credit card details from the DOM, and exfiltrates them via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in theft of payment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data from a checkout form is a hallmark of web skimming attacks and is never legitimate in a production e-commerce environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal checkout JavaScript should only process and transmit payment data to the legitimate payment processor, not to third-party or unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to payment gateways or fraud detection services, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Hooks into form submission events on payment pages
Reads sensitive fields (credit card number, CVV, expiration)
Sends data to an external, non-standard domain
Obfuscated or injected code not present in official Magento distribution

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Magento platform to gain write access to website files.
Malicious JavaScript skimmer is injected into the checkout or payment page template.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in user browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits payment information, the skimmer code intercepts the data and sends it to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into checkout or payment form submission events
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from client-side code to untrusted or unknown domains
Access to DOM elements containing payment or personal information
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in Magento template files (e.g., checkout.phtml, payment.phtml)
Presence of obfuscated or minified JavaScript not matching official Magento codebase
Injected <script> tags or inline event handlers in checkout-related pages
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout pages to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to Magento template files, especially those related to checkout or payment. Use web application firewalls or browser instrumentation to detect JavaScript that accesses payment fields and sends data to unknown domains. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for suspicious outbound requests. Regularly compare deployed JavaScript against known-good baselines.
